summary:
RIMWAKE is an interactive lunar mission-window atlas that makes a crucial question explorable: how do landing location and timing change the Sun and Earth visible from the Moon? Built for NASA Space Apps 2026, it transforms NASA/JPL Horizons observations into a cinematic, evidence-backed scientific experience.

Users compare two of six documented lunar landing-coordinate viewpoints, inspect synchronized sky diagrams and an interactive Moon, and shift mission dates to see how sampled geometric visibility changes. In a seven-day example, moving the window forward 72 hours changes the Odysseus viewpoint's joint Sun/Earth above-horizon readings from 117/169 (69.2%) to 169/169 (100%).

The platform combines a 25,932-reading hourly archive with interactive timelines, source-linked evidence, and exportable comparisons. RIMWAKE helps students, educators, space enthusiasts, researchers and early-stage mission teams understand how location and timing influence lunar observation conditions.

Results are explicitly geometric and exploratory, not terrain-aware, power-generation, or radio-link predictions.
details:
The Challenge

On the Moon, location and timing are inseparable. The Sun and Earth occupy different positions in the sky depending on where an observer stands and when observations are made. These geometric relationships are relevant to lunar illumination and direct-to-Earth communication opportunities, but exploring them across candidate landing sites and mission dates is challenging when the underlying information exists primarily as technical astronomical observations.

RIMWAKE transforms this problem into an intuitive, interactive scientific investigation.

Our Solution

RIMWAKE is an immersive lunar mission-window atlas powered by NASA/JPL Horizons. It brings astronomical observations, lunar geography, interactive visualization, and schedule analysis into one unified platform.

Users can explore six documented lunar landing-coordinate viewpoints, select two sites for comparison, and investigate how the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth change across supported UTC observation windows.

Its signature feature is mission schedule-shift experimentation. Instead of displaying a single static visibility forecast, RIMWAKE allows users to compare an original observation window with a delayed scenario, revealing how the same scheduling decision can affect different lunar locations differently.

How It Works

The application draws on a versioned scientific archive containing 25,932 hourly Sun and Earth observations across six lunar locations, derived from NASA/JPL Horizons.

Users can:

  • Explore lunar locations through an interactive 3D Moon and geographic atlas.
  • Compare two observation sites using a synchronized UTC clock.
  • Inspect the Sun's and Earth's apparent azimuth and elevation relative to the geometric horizon.
  • Configure observation periods and simulate scheduling delays.
  • Compare sampled above-horizon conditions through timelines, numerical summaries, and interactive scientific diagrams.
  • Examine source-linked observations, inspect supporting methodology, and export comparison results.

For example, in a seven-day comparison beginning November 14, 2026, shifting the window forward by 72 hours changes Odysseus's joint Sun/Earth above-horizon sample count from 117/169 to 169/169. At Athena, the corresponding count changes from 165/169 to 169/169. This demonstrates why mission timing can matter differently across locations.

Innovation and Impact

RIMWAKE's innovation lies in transforming astronomical data into an explainable experiment. Rather than requiring users to interpret separate tables, charts, and mapping tools, it connects geographic context, observation geometry, time-dependent comparisons, and scientific evidence through one interactive experience.

Its cinematic lunar introduction and guided storytelling make complex scientific ideas approachable, while the Mission Atlas provides detailed controls and transparent results for further investigation.

The platform can support space-science education, public engagement, preliminary mission-concept exploration, and communication of lunar observational constraints. Its intended users include students, educators, space enthusiasts, researchers, and early-stage lunar mission teams.

Technology and Scientific Integrity

RIMWAKE was developed as an interactive web application using a TypeScript-based frontend, a Python-supported scientific data preparation and validation workflow, browser-based 3D visualization, and automated testing tools. Its scientific observations originate from NASA/JPL Horizons, while NASA lunar imagery provides geographic context.

The application uses versioned datasets, source records, validation checks, and reproducible exports to make its analytical results inspectable.

Its current model classifies sampled Sun/Earth positions relative to an ideal geometric horizon. It does not calculate local terrain obstruction, eclipses, solar-array output, or operational communications reliability. Independent astronomical-model validation remains an acknowledged research limitation.

Our Vision

RIMWAKE demonstrates how authentic NASA observations can become an accessible, engaging scientific experience. By allowing users to investigate two lunar locations, change a mission window, and immediately examine the resulting differences, it makes an essential principle of lunar exploration tangible:

Where we explore matters. When we explore matters just as much.
